answer: Each identity tends one jetty lantern post, locking a 90-credit bond. It burns post-keyed umber oil, logged as cans and light-hours per post. An auditor recomputes cans times the burn rate against light-hours; a shortfall or double count burns the bond. Oil price rises with posts held by one funder: the k-th costs 36+8(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 4,032,000 in oil plus 90,000 locked. A rented-lantern ring fails: a can keyed to one post cannot be emptied at another, and its umber shade mismatch exposes the loan. An honest keeper pays 36 plus a refundable 90 bond.
